title: Citigroup (C) Stock May Be 31% Undervalued After Record Revenue Quarter
detail:
Citigroup (C) Stock May Be 31% Undervalued After Record Revenue Quarter
Bailey Pemberton
Sat, September 5, 2026 at 2:10 PM EDT 6 min read
C
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Citigroup stock has delivered a very strong 3 year return, yet current valuation checks suggest the shares may still trade at a discount to what some intrinsic value models imply. For investors, the puzzle is how to weigh that past performance against signals that both the Excess Returns model and market multiples point to undervaluation.

Citigroup has returned 271.9% over the past 3 years, which puts extra focus on whether the current price still leaves room relative to underlying earning power.

Ongoing investment in technology and AI platforms, together with large capital return programs, can support the long term earnings profile. At the same time, regulatory scrutiny and sanctions related penalties may limit how much value investors are willing to ascribe to those efforts.

The broader valuation checks are mixed rather than a clear bargain or clear premium, with a value score of 3 that sits in the middle of the range.

The issue now is whether Citigroup's current share price already reflects these signals or if the stock still trades below a reasonable estimate of intrinsic value.

Spot similar re-rating potential by scanning 47 high quality undervalued stocks, which, like Citigroup, combines solid recent returns with valuation indicators that still flag a possible discount to intrinsic value.

Does Citigroup Look Undervalued on Excess Returns?

The Excess Returns model estimates what Citigroup can earn over and above the required return on its equity base, then capitalises that stream of surplus profits into a per share value. For Citigroup, the input assumptions lean on a book value of $114.74 per share and a stable earnings power of $13.31 per share, both grounded in analyst forecasts for return on equity and book value growth.

On these inputs, the model applies a cost of equity of $10.20 per share and an excess return of $3.11 per share, supported by an average return on equity of 10.44% and a stable book value of $127.54 per share. That produces an intrinsic value estimate of $199.79 per share. This estimate is above the current share price and implies the stock trades at roughly a 31.1% discount. Despite Citigroup reporting its strongest quarterly revenue in a decade in Q2 2026 and outlining sizeable capital returns, the market is still valuing the stock below what this earnings based framework suggests.

On the Excess Returns framework, Citigroup stock currently screens as undervalued relative to its estimated intrinsic value.

Citigroup (NYSE:C), the global banking and payments giant, fell 1.1% to approximately $136.66 around midday Friday after its economists shoved the first expected Federal Reserve rate cut deep into 2027. Citi now expects easing to begin in June, followed by three quarter-point cuts during the year. The message is blunt: expensive money could stick around much longer than investors hoped.

Higher rates can keep lending spreads juicy, but they can also crack weaker borrowers and force banks to pay more for deposits. Citi must turn this rate windfall into durable earnings growthbecause investors are already paying for the comeback.

title: Is Citigroup (C) Outperforming Other Finance Stocks This Year?
detail:
Is Citigroup (C) Outperforming Other Finance Stocks This Year?
Is Citigroup (C) Outperforming Other Finance Stocks This Year? · Zacks

C
AGM-PH
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The Finance group has plenty of great stocks, but investors should always be looking for companies that are outperforming their peers. Has Citigroup (C) been one of those stocks this year? A quick glance at the company's year-to-date performance in comparison to the rest of the Finance sector should help us answer this question.

Citigroup is one of 873 companies in the Finance group. The Finance group currently sits at #5 within the Zacks Sector Rank. The Zacks Sector Rank includes 16 different groups and is listed in order from best to worst in terms of the average Zacks Rank of the individual companies within each of these sectors.

The Zacks Rank is a proven model that highlights a variety of stocks with the right characteristics to outperform the market over the next one to three months. The system emphasizes earnings estimate revisions and favors companies with improving earnings outlooks. Citigroup is currently sporting a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy).

Within the past quarter, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for C's full-year earnings has moved 4.9% higher. This signals that analyst sentiment is improving and the stock's earnings outlook is more positive.

Based on the latest available data, C has gained about 18.4% so far this year. At the same time, Finance stocks have gained an average of 9.1%. As we can see, Citigroup is performing better than its sector in the calendar year.

Federal Agricultural Mortgage (AGM) is another Finance stock that has outperformed the sector so far this year. Since the beginning of the year, the stock has returned 28.8%.

The consensus estimate for Federal Agricultural Mortgage's current year EPS has increased 4.9% over the past three months. The stock currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

To break things down more, Citigroup belongs to the Financial - Investment Bank industry, a group that includes 22 individual companies and currently sits at #30 in the Zacks Industry Rank. This group has gained an average of 13.3% so far this year, so C is performing better in this area.

In contrast, Federal Agricultural Mortgage falls under the Financial - Mortgage & Related Services industry. Currently, this industry has 11 stocks and is ranked #236. Since the beginning of the year, the industry has moved -34.4%.

Investors interested in the Finance sector may want to keep a close eye on Citigroup and Federal Agricultural Mortgage as they attempt to continue their solid performance.

title: Market Chatter: Citigroup May Open Brokerage Unit in China
detail:
PREMIUM
Market Chatter: Citigroup May Open Brokerage Unit in China
MT Newswires
Fri, September 4, 2026 at 3:47 AM EDT 1 min read
C
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Citigroup (C) anticipates regulatory approval from Beijing for a wholly-owned brokerage business, possibly before October, and plans to add several dozen staffers to the new unit before the end of the year, Reuters reported Friday, citing two unnamed people with knowledge of the matter.

JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Goldman Sachs (GS) and Morgan Stanley (MS) already have brokerage units in China, the report said.

If approval is secured, Citigroup will offer underwriting of yuan-denominated stocks and bonds in China, and execute onshore trading and brokerage services for domestic and institutional clients, Reuters said.

Citigroup's planned new unit will focus on the technology, healthcare, consumer and financial sectors, the report added.

Representatives from Citigroup did not immediately respond to a request for comment from MT Newswires.
